column1:
Updated assessment incorporating Beige Book references:

- Macro tone (FOMC): Labor market continued to strengthen while Q1 growth slowdown seen as transitory; moderate expansion expected with inflation near 2 percent, though core softened and market-based inflation compensation remains low.

- Beige Book cross-check:
  - Economic activity: Increased across Districts with continued expansion in manufacturing, but growth varied across consumer spending and freight shipments growth slowed.
  - Labor supply: Labor demand remains strong and tight labor markets are restraining growth in manufacturing, transportation, and construction, pointing to capacity constraints rather than weak demand.
  - Prices/costs: Input cost pressures are feeding into selling prices, consistent with some pipeline inflation pressure even as recent core readings softened.
  - Wages: Tight labor markets are influencing wages upward, though pace remains moderate in most reports.

- Credit conditions (SLOOS lens):
  - C&I: Standards broadly little changed to slightly easier; demand not robust at many banks.
  - CRE: Tighter standards and softer demand across categories.
  - Consumer: Tighter auto credit; some easing in credit cards and improved willingness to lend on other consumer loans; net mixed, with autos a drag.
  - Foreign banks: Somewhat tighter via higher spreads/lower LTVs.

- Policy/risks: Beige Book labor constraints and freight softness, plus SLOOS tightening in CRE and autos and tepid loan demand, tilt risks modestly more cautious than the macro-only view. Still, broad District growth and manufacturing expansion support continued gradual normalization with close monitoring of inflation and financial conditions.

Net effect: Modestly positive outlook, but more cautious given labor-capacity constraints and mixed demand/credit signals.
